title: When Retrieval Is Not Enough: Obsolete Facts in Agent Memory
trick: Hold the reader, prompt, newest fact and four-statement evidence size fixed; swap one unrelated memory for the fact's obsolete version: a 7B model falls from 100% to 44.6%, every error picking the stale value.
framing_stripped: Called 'when retrieval is not enough: obsolete facts in agent memory', a separation of retrieval failure from use failure; it is (a) a one-model BM25 budget sweep on a 100-question synthetic memory benchmark in which both versions of the target fact are already retrieved at every budget, so the decline is a reader effect by construction (sec. 3.1, App. E), and (b) a 74-question paired A/B swap of one zero-overlap distractor for the obsolete value of the target, at temperature 0 on two Qwen models (sec. 3.2, Table 16), where in all 50 flips listed in Table 17 the obsolete value is the ordinary-world fact and the 'latest' is a synthetic falsehood.
method_equations: Evidence set at budget $b$ (sec. 2, App. A.4): rank statements $s$ of the history $H$ by BM25 score $\mathrm{bm25}(q, s)$ for question $q$, take the longest ranked prefix whose token count fits, and restore chronological order: $E_b(q) = \mathrm{chron}\{s_{(1)}, \dots, s_{(k)}\}$ with $k = \max\{k : \sum_{i \le k} |s_{(i)}| \le b\}$, $|s|$ the token length; budgets $b \in \{64, 128, 256, 512\}$ give mean $k$ of $4.17, 8.57, 16.99, 33.60$ on the 6K history (Table 7). Equal-size intervention (sec. 2): for each of the 74 conflict questions, condition $A = \{s^{+}, u_1, u_2, u_3\}$ and condition $B = \{s^{-}, s^{+}, u_1, u_2\}$, where $s^{+}$ is the latest (highest-numbered) statement about the target relation, $s^{-}$ its older conflicting version, and $u_j$ unrelated statements chosen deterministically with zero content-word overlap with $q$ and outside the update chain; prompt sizes differ by under one token between A and B (App. G). Outcome $y_c(q) \in \{0, 1\}$ is normalized substring match of the answer against the benchmark gold under condition $c$; each answer is also classed as latest / stale / unknown / other against the reconstructed chain values (App. A.5). Paired test: with discordant counts $n_{A} = \#\{q : y_A = 1, y_B = 0\}$ and $n_{B} = \#\{q : y_A = 0, y_B = 1\}$, the exact two-sided McNemar $p$-value is the binomial tail $p = 2 \sum_{i \le \min(n_A, n_B)} \binom{n_A + n_B}{i} 2^{-(n_A + n_B)}$ (capped at 1). Observed (Table 16): Qwen2.5-7B $n_A = 41$, $n_B = 0$, accuracy $74/74 \to 33/74$ ($100 \to 44.6$), $p = 9.09 \times 10^{-13}$; Qwen3-14B $n_A = 9$, $n_B = 0$, $74/74 \to 65/74$ ($100 \to 87.8$), $p = 0.0039$; all $41 + 9 = 50$ flips classed stale. Budget sweep (Tables 1, 8, 11, 18): 6K accuracy $45, 40, 36, 32$ at $b = 64, 128, 256, 512$; conflict stratum $19/74, 15/74, 12/74, 9/74$, no-conflict $26/26, 25/26, 24/26, 23/26$; paired $64$ vs $512$: $n_{64} = 14$, $n_{512} = 1$, $p = 9.77 \times 10^{-4}$; 32K: $69/100$ vs $58/100$, $n_{64} = 18$, $n_{512} = 7$, $p = 0.0433$; gold-assisted support (the latest statement is in $E_b$) $100/100$ at every budget. Baselines (Table 4, 11): question-only $19/100$ ($0/74$ conflict, $19/26$ no-conflict); full 6K history in context $37/100$; gold-isolated one-statement evidence $97/100$ (different prompt).
load_bearing_assumption: That the harm comes from $s^{-}$ being the superseded version of the target rather than from $s^{-}$ being the model's prior: the benchmark replaces true facts with synthetic ones, so in every one of the 50 flips in Table 17 the 'obsolete' value is ordinary world knowledge (Japan $\to$ Japanese, Australia $\to$ Canberra, Microsoft $\to$ Satya Nadella) and the 'latest' contradicts it, and the question-only model answers 0/74 conflict questions and 19/26 no-conflict questions (Table 11). The authors say so: the results 'establish susceptibility to these competitors, not that temporal obsolescence alone drives the effect' (sec. 4). If prior strength is the cause, the paper measures how much an in-context falsehood loses to a parametric fact when the fact is also quoted in context, and says nothing about an agent's own stale notes, which have no parametric backing.
weakest_component: The identification of 'obsolete' with 'prior-consistent' is total and unmatched: no counterbalanced arm (world fact as the latest, synthetic value as the obsolete) and no unfamiliar-entity arm exist, though both are named (sec. 4), so a critic reads the 55.4-point drop as context-versus-prior, a known effect, with the recency instruction losing to the prior. Second, the 74 intervention questions 'were also used for prompt development and the pilot' and the comparison is 'a within-cohort paired comparison rather than held-out confirmation' (sec. 2); third, one history per benchmark size, temperature 0, one decode per cell, so there is no variance over seeds or histories and the McNemar $p$-values describe 'this benchmark instance rather than a population' (App. A.5); fourth, the scoring metric is substring match with documented false positives ('rugby union' counted correct for gold 'rugby' while stating the stale value) and two mixed outputs containing both values counted as latest (App. I.1); fifth, the budget-sweep mechanism ('additional evidence appears to compound an already difficult selection', sec. 3.1) is observational and the 6K-vs-32K accuracy levels differ by 24 points at the same budget for reasons the paper does not analyze (Table 1).
regime: Readers: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen3-14B (think=false), served by Ollama, temperature 0, seed 42, num_ctx 2048, num_predict 64 for the final runs (App. A.2). Data: MemoryAgentBench Conflict_Resolution split, FactConsolidation single-hop: 6K history of 455 numbered statements and 100 questions (74 with one older conflicting statement, 26 without; chains of length at most two), 32K history of 2,310 statements and 100 questions (63 conflict / 37 no-conflict by automated chain labels, two ambiguous). Retrieval: BM25 over single statements, budgets 64 to 512 evidence tokens (4 to 34 statements), prompts of 157 to 624 tokens. Accuracy bands: 32 to 45% (6K sweep), 58 to 69% (32K), 44.6 to 100% (intervention). Scale: about 1,500 completed model calls across the inventory (Table 3), one university GPU server; no agent loop, no tools, no multi-turn interaction, no memory system beyond BM25 over a statement store.
information_asymmetry: (1) Write time vs read time: whether $s^{-}$ is superseded is known at write time (a later statement about the same relation exists in the store) and is recoverable post hoc by chain reconstruction, but BM25 ranking is version-blind and the reader is asked to recover supersession from statement numbers alone; the paper's recommendation to 'retire, down-weight, or explicitly mark superseded facts as inactive while preserving provenance and validity information' (sec. 4) is exactly moving that bit from the audit stage to the store, and no arm tests it. (2) Construction vs analysis: the benchmark builder knows, per question, whether the obsolete value equals the world fact; the analysis never stratifies on it, and the counterbalanced arm that would separate recency from prior is named and not run (sec. 4). (3) Post-hoc vs deployable: the 'support' audit uses the gold answer to find the latest statement (sec. 2, App. A.4); a deployable detector of 'both versions retrieved' does not exist in the paper, so a memory system cannot yet raise the flag this paper says it should. (4) For CL-W43-05 (compaction summaries fail by unsourced persistence, not by length): this paper is the reader-side cell of that claim with the source present. It settles that a superseded value sitting beside the current one, under an explicit recency rule the prompt states, is selected over the current one in 41/74 (7B) and 9/74 (14B) cases at matched size, and that one competing statement is worse than three unrelated ones of the same size, so a length control alone does not explain a stale-selection failure, which is evidence on the 'not by length' half of the claim; it also says a provenance marker in the form of a statement number is not consumed reliably by 7B to 14B readers, which weighs against C-W43-09's 'label instead of delete' arm and for SJC's delete. It leaves open everything the claim is actually about: the stale values here were observed facts with a source, not unsourced persistence (a claim no observation supports), so the commission cell of CL-W43-05 is untouched; the competitor here is backed by the model's parametric prior, which an agent's own stale plan bullet is not; the store is a numbered statement list, not a compaction summary; the models are two small Qwen readers; and whether an explicit 'inactive' tag (rather than an implicit number) is consumed is the untested arm. The transferable piece is the ruler: a matched-size swap of one unrelated entry for the stale entry inside a summary, scored by exact match on the next action's argument, is a judge-free closure-cell probe that CL-W43-05 did not have.
occupies: Published, on MemoryAgentBench FactConsolidation single-hop with Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-14B: that at matched four-statement size under a frozen chronology prompt, replacing one unrelated statement with the obsolete version of the target drops accuracy from 100% to 44.6% and 87.8% with all 50 paired flips selecting the stale value; that growing the BM25 budget from 64 to 512 tokens lowers accuracy (45% to 32% at 6K, 69% to 58% at 32K) while the latest statement is retrieved in 100/100 sets at every budget; and the 'retrieved but not used' decomposition on this benchmark. For CL-W43-05 this occupies the sentence 'a superseded value present beside the current one overrides it at the reader even with recency metadata' for retrieved, sourced memories; the claim can no longer own 'readers ignore version marks' as a new finding and keeps only the compaction-summary case, the unsourced (never-observed) case, and the matched-length test inside a summary.

neighbors.title: Reliable Post-Retrieval Assembly for Agent Memory: Separating Evidence Extraction from Policy Execution (cited by this paper under its earlier title 'Don't ask the LLM to track freshness')
neighbors.trick: Split answering into an LLM step that extracts the matching evidence into a candidate list and a separate step that applies the answer rule (take the highest serial number); on the same FactConsolidation task single-hop rises to 82 to 93%, and a targeted swap shows the freshness executor itself adds 2 points, the separation the rest; this card's paper holds the pipeline fixed and varies only evidence composition.

neighbors.title: STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
neighbors.trick: Write 400 scenarios in which a later observation invalidates an earlier memory without saying so, and probe whether the model detects the outdated state, rejects a query that presupposes it, and acts on the new state; best model 55.2%; this card's paper tests explicit numbered contradictions, not implicit ones.

neighbors.title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions (MemoryAgentBench)
neighbors.trick: Feed long-context datasets to an agent incrementally, turn by turn, and score four memory competencies (accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, selective forgetting); FactConsolidation is its selective-forgetting split and the sole data source of this card's paper.

neighbors.title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
neighbors.trick: Add irrelevant sentences to grade-school math problems and measure the accuracy drop; this card's paper uses the same kind of unrelated statement as the control arm and shows it is far less harmful than one competing version of the target.

neighbors.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
neighbors.trick: Move the relevant document through the positions of a long context and show accuracy is highest at the ends and lowest in the middle; this card's paper restores chronological order and never varies position, so position is an unexamined covariate of its budget sweep.

theme_fit.why: a lossy memory store measured at the read stage for what it costs, with a matched-size ruler; the direct reader-side neighbour of CL-W43-05 (what a stale entry beside the current one does to the reader)
a benchmark-validity point (end-to-end memory scores collapse retrieval and use) and a paired equal-size instrument that separates them; supplies the ruler, not the agent loop
no training, no credit, no agent RL

limitations_as_complaints: I cannot tell whether my reader prefers the old fact because it is old or because it is true: 'In this benchmark, obsolete values often match familiar world knowledge while the synthetic updates contradict it. Our results therefore establish susceptibility to these competitors, not that temporal obsolescence alone drives the effect' (sec. 4); the counterbalanced arm is named and not run.

I have no deployable way to know when my retriever has handed the reader both versions of a fact: 'The gold-assisted audits are diagnostic rather than deployable retrieval evaluations' (sec. 4) and the support check 'is therefore a diagnostic, not a deployable retrieval procedure' (sec. 2), so the flag this paper says a memory system should raise cannot yet be raised.

My result is two small Qwen readers over a lexical index: 'Our study is limited to two open-weight Qwen models, deterministic decoding, one synthetic benchmark, single-hop chains of length at most two, and lexical retrieval. We therefore do not establish the same behavior for dense retrieval, multi-hop memory, or end-to-end systems such as Mem0' (sec. 4).
